title: Runtime function guardrails and invoke UX: lightweight validation, streaming adapters, and cross-SDK ergonomics
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Developers using function/tool calling across SDKs run into three categories of friction: 1) noisy runtime errors from slight schema mismatches, 2) awkward streaming ergonomics when function results are large or emitted incrementally, and 3) inconsistent retry semantics across Python/TS/Go.

Goal: Deliver a small, consistent set of client-side helpers and runtime guardrails that (a) perform fast, opt-in validation at call time, (b) provide streaming invocation adapters (sync/async) that support backpressure and checkpointed resume, and (c) expose a single retry contract that maps to the platform's server-side idempotency and fallback behavior. Keep server footprint minimal: prefer client-side validation + server-side authoritative checks + graceful fallback when strictness is relaxed.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) expose a common minimal API for function invocation with the same semantics documented in the SDK guide
Lightweight schema validators run synchronously before network send and optionally in strict/lenient modes; strict mode blocks invocation if mismatch detected
stream_invoke or equivalent returns idiomatic streams/async iterators in each SDK and supports resume via checkpoint token
Retry policy config is unified across SDKs and respects server-provided idempotency tokens and retry-after signals
Integration tests cover schema validation mismatches, large streaming responses (>=50MB), and mid-stream resume after simulated network failure
Docs and migration guide published under docs/sdk/function-calling with examples for all three languages
design_notes: High-level approach: deliver two complementary layers - (A) Declarative FunctionSpec (lightweight shape + optional coercion rules) that SDKs can compile to fast runtime checks; (B) Invoke helpers (invoke, stream_invoke) that wrap network, apply validators, handle idempotency, and surface ergonomic iterators/streams.

FunctionSpec shape: name:string, params: JSON Schema subset (type, required, enum, properties up to depth 2), coerce: boolean, strict: boolean. Keep schema subset intentionally small to avoid heavy deps (no $ref, no allOf).

Validation modes: 'none' (default), 'warn' (client logs validation mismatch but proceeds), 'strict' (throws locally and does not call network), 'auto-coerce' (attempts safe coercions: numeric strings -> numbers, trim whitespace).

Server interaction: server still validates full schema and returns structured error codes. SDK will translate server validation error into a ValidationError subtype that includes server-provided field path suggestions.

Retry contract: SDK exposes RetryConfig {max_attempts:int, backoff:exponential jitter, allowed_on: [network,error_code], idempotency_key: optional}. If idempotency_key unset, SDK auto-generates for idempotent function calls and omits for non-idempotent (developer must opt-in). Server supports idempotency-key header and maps to stable retries/fallbacks.
Streaming: stream_invoke returns an ergonomic handle per language:

- Python: StreamInvokeIterator (async for / sync iterator wrappers). Supports .checkpoint() -> opaque token and .resume(token) -> resumes from server-provided checkpoint. Uses small resumable chunks (server returns checkpoint every 64KB or logical event).
- TypeScript: AsyncIterable plus helper createStreamReader() that exposes read() returning {done, value, checkpoint?}. Also provide fromStream(stream) to adapt Node streams and Web Streams.
- Go: io.ReadCloser-like StreamReader with Context; supports Resume(ctx, token) call and exposes Checkpoint() (string).

Backpressure and chunking: clients expose a pull-based API. Under the hood the runtime will request tokens in batches sized by SDK-configured window (default 4 messages). This minimizes memory spikes for large outputs and harmonizes latency across SDKs.

Open questions: whether to expand schema subset for nested arrays/objects (we defer for now to depth 2). Also debate on autogeneration of idempotency keys for side-effectful function calls - current decision: require explicit opt-in for non-idempotent endpoints.
Security: validator code must never leak sensitive parameter values into logs when validation warnings are emitted (masking policy).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-2): implement FunctionSpec in each SDK with shared test vectors. Deliver a small codegen that converts FunctionSpec -> runtime validator. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-monorepo/pull/4856
Phase 2 (week 3): build invoke + retry primitives (common logic in TS core lib used to produce Py/Go bindings). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-monorepo/pull/4891
Phase 3 (week 4): streaming adapters with checkpoint token protocol and resume tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-monorepo/pull/4920
Phase 4 (week 5): cross-language integration tests, docs, examples, and upload to package registries

Implementation notes: use a tiny vendored runtime validator (BSD-licensed) in each repo to avoid pulling heavy schema libs. Keep runtime in a single TS file compiled down to minimal artifacts for Python & Go (via codegen).
Owner(s): Marcus (core + typescript), Lina Gomez (python runtime), Harish Rao (go bindings), QA: Daniel Park
testing_plan: Unit tests for validator: mismatch patterns, coercion cases, masked logging behavior
Contract tests: symmetrical accept/reject cases across Py/TS/Go using the same FunctionSpec fixtures
Integration tests against staging runtime with fault injection: mid-stream disconnect, partial server validation failures, server-requested slowdown (429 retry-after), idempotency replays

Performance tests: measure overhead of client-side validation on cold path (target <2ms per invocation for small schemas), and memory usage for streaming large payloads (target <50MB resident for 100MB response)
E2E sample app: chat-with-tools example updated to use resume on network flakiness and explicit strict validation setting
rollout_plan: Canary: release to dev-only SDK channel + flag in console to route 5% of requests through new client-side validators
Beta: enable by default in SDKs with validation mode 'warn' for 2 weeks and gather telemetry on warn->strict adoption
GA: default mode 'none' but provide CLI to opt-in to 'auto-coerce' or 'strict' for projects
Migration: provide docs + one-click codemod snippets for common patterns (JS/TS) to replace existing ad-hoc invocation wrappers
Monitor: instrument validation warning rate, streaming resume success rate, retry loop counts, and end-to-end latency impact
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: client-side validator may diverge from server semantics -> Mitigation: keep validator subset intentionally small and maintain shared canonical test fixtures; server remains authoritative and SDK surfaces server errors clearly
Risk: checkpoint tokens leak internal state -> Mitigation: tokens are opaque, HMAC-signed blobs with short TTL, stored server-side mapping if needed
Risk: added complexity in SDKs leads to breaking changes for users -> Mitigation: default to permissive behavior (warn/none) and provide thorough migration docs
Risk: performance overhead -> Mitigation: microbenchmarks in CI, lazy validation compilation, and caching compiled validators per-FunctionSpec
